problems.source_says: The source defines this variable as a literal character count. Codebook section 6 defines automated_score as a scoring model for creativity, including semantic-distance tests and language-model judges. It provides neither a mechanical-character-count category nor permission to substitute the closest code. The form acknowledges that no creativity-scoring model was used, so its automated_score label is unsupported under the supplied definition; the elaboration construct remains supported.
problems.quote: Number of characters is the length of the text measured in characters.
problems.locator: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 11), Table 1 notes; PDF p. 23 (printed p. 20), Table 5 column (2). creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Measure, line 98; elaboration definition, line 82.

problems.source_says: DAT averages semantic distances among words supplied by one participant, measuring within-person associative variety. Although the flexibility table entry mentions category counts, the codebook explicitly states that variety among one person's own ideas is flexibility, and the screening brief repeats that rule. The form's rationale for other, that DAT is not a literal category count, conflicts with this explicit within-person-variety rule. Under that rule the construct should be flexibility; automated_score and after_ai remain supported.
problems.quote: computed as the average semantic distance (ranging from 0 to 100) between the words provided by the participant, with higher values indicating greater divergent thinking ability.
problems.locator: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 11), Table 1 notes, definition of DAT score. creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Construct, lines 81 and 87, especially the explicit within-person-variety rule.
